confidence_notes: Restaurant and coffee anchors rest on two aggregated cost-of-living sources (NZ$4-6 cappuccino, NZ$15-25 inexpensive meal, NZ$60-100 mid-range meal for two) plus one three-course listing at NZ$75 per adult, and are medium quality. Beer (NZ$7-12 range) is medium. Cocktail and wine have no direct price evidence; both are inferred from the beer anchor (cocktail about 1.7x beer, wine glass about 1.25x beer). Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak ski season, with no booking pages inspected. The FX rate is taken from a search summary of the RBA exchange-rates table for 2026-10-16; I did not open the RBA page directly. The NZD-to-USD conversion used for the NZD-based figures is my own assumption of about 0.62 USD per NZD, not a sourced rate, so all USD food and drink anchors carry that uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used directly. Basis is Queenstown's own NZD price points from cost-of-living sources, with the restaurant benchmark cross-checked against Wellington (Queenstown restaurants about 9% higher). Cocktail and wine use the beer relationship described above. Accommodation reflects general knowledge of Queenstown's winter-season pricing, with dorm and private hostel rooms set against the hotel tiers.
